negative_findings.description: No Kosovo Competition Authority decision specifically on bank commissions, interchange fees or account fees was identified. Albanian-language searches for 'Autoriteti i Konkurrencës vendim bankat komisionet' returned almost exclusively Albania's Autoriteti i Konkurrencës (caa.gov.al) cases against Albanian banks (e.g. Vendim 174, Raiffeisen/BKT investigations), not Kosovo's AKK.
negative_findings.result_summary: Kosovo AKK decisions register exists at ak.rks-gov.net/vendimet, but no banking/payments fee case surfaced in search results; publicised AKK cases in results concerned other sectors (e.g. fuel/NAFTA).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The interchange/fee enforcement channel appears dormant or unindexed in Kosovo, so competition-authority output cannot yet be assumed as a fee-intelligence stream; the register must be enumerated directly rather than searched.

negative_findings.description: Albanian-language queries about Kosovo consumer/competition/ombudsperson topics are dominated by Republic of Albania institutions with near-identical names (Autoriteti i Konkurrencës, Avokati i Popullit) and domains (.gov.al, avokatipopullit.gov.al).
negative_findings.result_summary: Multiple searches returned Albanian rather than Kosovar institutions on the first page.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Automated collection must domain-pin to .rks-gov.net / oik-rks.org / bqk-kos.org, or the corpus will silently fill with Albania data and corrupt Kosovo conclusions.

negative_findings.description: No centralised, official comparison table of bank fees/tariffs across all Kosovo banks was found (no BQK equivalent of, e.g., CBCG's 'Tarife banaka' comparison page in Montenegro, which did surface in the sr search).
negative_findings.result_summary: Fee disclosure in Kosovo is decentralised to each bank's own çmimorja PDF/page; the regional comparator that exists in Montenegro has no Kosovo counterpart in results.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Cross-bank fee benchmarking requires assembling per-bank PDFs and normalising them; there is no single authoritative feed to track.

negative_findings.description: Serbian-language (sr) searching returned useful CBK material (Godišnji izveštaj, finansijsko obrazovanje, žalbe terminology) but no Serbian-language Kosovo consumer-protection NGO, complaint portal, or bank tariff publication aimed at the Serb-majority market.
negative_findings.result_summary: sr-language coverage of this cell is essentially limited to CBK's own translated publications.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Conduct and pricing intelligence for Serb-majority municipalities (and parallel-banking realities) is likely invisible in the sq/en corpus.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated financial ombudsman / alternative dispute resolution (ADR) body for banking disputes was identified for Kosovo; complaint escalation appears to end at BQK's consumer complaints division, with the general Ombudsperson covering public authorities and courts handling the rest.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches for an ombudsperson-banking link returned the general Avokati i Popullit institution only.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Absence of a financial ADR body means dispute-outcome data (rulings against named banks) is largely unavailable — BQK aggregates are the ceiling of available granularity.

coverage_gaps.description: AKK's decisions register (ak.rks-gov.net/vendimet) was identified but its contents were not enumerated; whether any banking/payments case exists is unresolved.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Crawl and enumerate every decision and concentration entry on ak.rks-gov.net, then keyword-filter on bankë, pagesa, kartelë, komision, tarifë, interchange, POS.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate the BQK register of licensed banks/PSPs/MFIs and locate each institution's çmimorja / cenovnik / price-list URL; archive dated PDFs.

coverage_gaps.description: Court decisions on bank-consumer disputes (Gjykata Themelore/Apelit, and the Kosovo case-law portal) were not searched in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search Kosovo judiciary portals (gjyqesori-rks.org, supreme court case-law databases) in sq and sr for bank fee, loan-contract and unfair-term litigation.

coverage_gaps.description: EU accession/progress reporting and IFI assessments (European Commission Kosovo Report, World Bank/IMF FSAP-style notes) that evaluate consumer protection and competition enforcement in Kosovo's financial sector were not collected.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add EC Kosovo Report chapters on consumer protection (Ch. 28) and competition (Ch. 8) plus World Bank financial-consumer-protection diagnostics to the source set.

coverage_gaps.description: A machine-readable or standalone BQK complaint-statistics publication (beyond narrative passages inside annual reports) was not found.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Check BQK statistics/publications sections and, if absent, consider a formal information request for the complaints time series by institution and complaint type.

brief: Kosovo's consumer-accountability layer for banking is anchored almost entirely on the Central Bank (BQK): its consumer-protection division, the ankesat.bqk-kos.org intake system, and the complaints chapters of its Albanian and Serbian annual reports provide the only continuous complaint time series (roughly 350 complaints in 2014 rising to ~1,200/year by 2019-2025). Fee transparency is decentralised — there is no official cross-bank comparison table, so each bank's effective-dated çmimorja PDF (ProCredit, NLB, TEB located; most others still to be found) must be archived and diffed individually, with the PSD2-aligned draft Law on Payment Services and BQK's basic-payment-account and interbank-payments regulations defining what must be published. The competition channel exists institutionally (Autoriteti Kosovar i Konkurrencës decisions and merger registers) but no bank-fee or interchange decision surfaced in search, so it is a register to enumerate rather than a proven stream. Two practical hazards dominate: heavy name collision with Republic of Albania institutions in Albanian-language search, and near-absent Serbian-language material beyond CBK's own translations.
